## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.

Fixes: the Gateway cleanup scheduled task briefly shows a console or taskbar entry when its once-per-minute action starts.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: automatic Gateway cleanup continues without interrupting the desktop. The cleanup cadence, current-user identity and cleanup policy remain unchanged. This ships with Companion, not Gateway-only repackaging.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The task currently launches Windows PowerShell directly with `-WindowStyle Hidden`. A console can be created before PowerShell handles that option.

The task instead starts a small .NET Framework 4.8 GUI-subsystem helper. It launches the existing PowerShell worker with creation-time `CreateNoWindow`, drains output, records failure diagnostics and returns the worker exit code. The hash-versioned helper and worker are copied outside the Companion package. Natural cleanup after real bundle removal is now verified for the qualified combined candidate below; uninstall window-event collection remains blocked.

Both this helper (A) and the evaluated JScript prototype met the measured visible-window/taskbar contract. A avoids adding WSH/JScript/COM policy dependence. It does add a small custom executable and build wiring; that executable can itself be blocked by application control. The JScript prototype is not included in this PR.

The signing follow-up signs the cleanup EXE through the existing Azure Artifact Signing identity **before** x64, ARM64 and Store/Dev MSIX builds embed it. Signing the outer SetupEngine DLL cannot sign an embedded EXE. Non-dev Release builds now require signed input by default; unsigned Debug/Dev builds and explicitly non-published PR smoke builds remain supported. Pre-embed signature checks, post-build resource byte/signature checks and final payload verification prevent an unsigned or substituted nested helper from silently reaching a signed release.

### Current-head signed native acceptance: `9c521dd8e0e1e0f5397148f4d30935f80f5db1fa`

The three commits after `d3a9bc46` correct tests/observers only; the sign-before-embed product implementation is unchanged. This exact head now passes actual signed-helper execution, correlated enforcing-policy controls and finalized uninstall visibility in a disposable native x64 guest. These results supersede the corresponding earlier proof blockers below, without rewriting failed attempts as passes.

Provider/target/mode: **Hyper-V / Windows / normal**, lease `cbx_0bada2c7f851`. No hosted run URL exists for this local Hyper-V run. Proof CLI pin `6bd7156a`, executable SHA256 `02E320F040005AE40C6F4445FECB3948F4FF762B2B7786FCAE29A9B80B4C2F40`. Actual release helper was built, signed with a **guest-only test signer**, then embedded through `OpenClawSignedCleanupHostPath` and `RequireSignedCleanupHost=true`. The shipped verifier and an independent extraction verified the actual named resource: Authenticode Valid and byte-identical signed/extracted SHA256 `3925A87C6912C405DA84D4A5FDC9081DAD9EDD3A1B2EDACC26F1C752C203F02B`. Release SetupEngine SHA256 `07DC4F9CEA1EB412DA26272F120807E8394E4973CD4CD9109D7D5E37AC7EA08A`. This is not Azure production signing or Store signing.

**AppLocker ENFORCE:** policy application was qualified with event **8001** and a record-ID boundary. The actual extracted signed helper returned **37**, produced its intended fixture effect and correlated to event **8002**. Unsigned and wrong-signer controls both failed with native **1260**, produced no forbidden effect and correlated to distinct **8004** events. Records were reconciled from the EXE and DLL channel by exact provider, path, target user, rule and process identity; no requirement or timeout was relaxed. All three controls passed. Original policy was restored.

**Real uninstall lifecycle:** production deployment and actual Task Scheduler invoked the signed resource after real disposable MSIX removal. An adjacent wrapper synchronized entry; the untouched production cleanup worker then ran. Actual GUI helper parent and worker were observed through final release/exit, helper native exit **0**, production complete marker present, task retired. Finalized observer: **294 window samples, 15 taskbar samples, zero visible-console/taskbar observations, zero observer errors**, 9.368 seconds. Maximum measured gaps: window **674.04 ms**, taskbar **1234.25 ms**. This is bounded sampled no-flash proof, not a guarantee against every shorter transient or a full Store Companion settings-migration pass.

The proof owner copied current-head receipts/TRX and restored guest policy, removed owned tasks/packages/processes, and released the exact lease (stop exit 0, nonexpired); no host/shared Gateway state was changed. Receipt manifest binds the final evidence JSON to SHA256 `5069093D48C53DC177DCB0DF07647775E9E53E2E4514D413AC11789F8AFB393D`. Raw archives remain private; only sanitized copied outcomes are published here.

**Limits:** Smart App Control reputation is not covered. ARM64: the development-signed ARM64 MSIX installs on native ARM64 Windows build 28661, and the pinned installed files match the signed package hashes. Signed-helper and application-control execution are verified on x64 only. ARM64 cleanup runtime behavior with an unsigned local build is covered by the native ARM64 run below, which also explains the earlier harness `0x80070005`.

ARM64 receipt summary SHA256s (2026-10-27, exact head `9c521dd8`): `6D442360F0105D0BC7162918C066D8A413E1103612533F08E87F1EA3EF9294C7` and `3DCCE7F0CC6DADF7B72628977D4A1EB88E926291EC74D69A3B4CA66376418FB6`. The later run captured an owner-SID, session-1, medium-integrity, non-elevated, non-AppContainer tools token; the load was still denied, so the earlier elevation hypothesis was not supported. Machine-state restoration passed; the earlier controller-local absent-versus-empty environment rollback discrepancy is recorded separately. Official-signed install/upgrade/uninstall will run on the first prerelease containing this change, before stable promotion. Broader AV/EDR diversity and the historical reporter-build/settings-migration limitations remain; no blanket proof-pool completion is claimed.

### Current-head native ARM64 host run: `9c521dd8e0e1e0f5397148f4d30935f80f5db1fa`

Native ARM64 Windows build 28661, interactive desktop with the standard taskbar visible, unelevated owner session. Exact clean detached worktree; `.\build.ps1` produced Debug `win-arm64` output, so the embedded helper is the **unsigned** development build (embedded and deployed SHA256 `D0490CDA3FB05A40532F4C6C6C1F32E10A750D31316E7E0C28BE13B0D5D9643B`). Deployment used the built SetupEngine's own `GatewayPackageCleanup.DeployAsync`; the earlier external validation kit was not used. Only nonce-named tasks, scratch folders and one disposable fixture package were used. Tasks, the fixture package, test certificates and cleanup folders were removed afterward, and the uninstall lane's before/after inventory matched.

**Observer calibration:** the checked-in observer detected a deliberately visible classic console on all three channels: 1 WinEvent, 86 window-sample and 2 taskbar UI Automation on-screen observations; 88 window and 4 taskbar samples; zero observer errors. An earlier run with the host taskbar hidden failed this positive control as designed; everything below ran with the taskbar visible.

**Actual Scheduler:** the production `cleanup-task.ps1` registered uniquely named tasks with the deployed helper as the action, the family as its only argument, an Interactive/Limited principal and the PT1M time plus logon triggers. The triggers were then removed so only the observed start could run each task. With an event-synchronized synthetic worker, Scheduler `LastTaskResult` was **0** and **37**; in the 37 case the helper recorded the worker's stderr in `cleanup-host-error.txt`. Finalized observer: **zero window or taskbar observations** in both cases, 262/243 window samples, 10/8 taskbar samples, zero observer errors.

**Real uninstall lifecycle:** a minimal disposable fixture MSIX was signed with a run-only test certificate, trusted temporarily in LocalMachine TrustedPeople through a bounded same-user UAC child, and installed for the current user. The production `cleanup.ps1 -Register` ran with no ownership flags, so `owned.json` held no distro, install path or native package. With the observer live, its starter ran real `Remove-AppxPackage`, confirmed the package absent, and started the real task 113 ms later. The checked-in synchronization wrapper, reached through a small adjacent launcher because the helper passes only `-Family`, then ran the byte-identical deployed worker. Helper exit **0**, `cleanup-result.txt` `complete`, `owned.json` removed, task self-retired, package absent, helper present with an unchanged hash, worker hash unchanged. Finalized observer: **382 window samples, 14 taskbar samples, zero window/taskbar observations, zero observer errors**. All 23 lane criteria passed.

**Architecture finding:** the helper is a PE32 AnyCPU .NET Framework 4.8 image and runs under **x64 emulation** on this host, not natively: `GetProcessInformation(ProcessMachineTypeInfo)` reports `0x8664`, with `xtajit64se.dll` and the `Framework64` CLR loaded. The Windows PowerShell worker it starts also runs as x64 (same evidence; `RuntimeInformation.ProcessArchitecture` is `X64`). The same `powershell.exe` started from a native ARM64 parent runs `Arm64` with the `FrameworkArm64` CLR, so on ARM64 this change likely moves the per-minute worker from native to x64-emulated Windows PowerShell; main's direct Scheduler launch was not separately measured. Cleanup behavior above is correct under emulation. A native ARM64 helper was not evaluated. `IsWow64Process2` reports `0x0000`/`0xAA64` for both processes, which only excludes x86 WOW64.

**Limits:** unsigned local Debug build; signed-helper, AppLocker and Smart App Control acceptance on ARM64 are not covered. `DeployAsync` ran from an unpackaged process, not from an installed Companion MSIX. Exit lanes used a synthetic worker. The fixture is not a real Gateway, so no WSL or native Gateway removal ran. Maximum measured gaps across the four observed runs: window 32.30 to 39.35 ms, taskbar 535.36 to 540.53 ms; this is bounded sampled no-flash proof, not a guarantee against shorter transients. The earlier harness `0x80070005` was a package-identity boundary: from an unpackaged process, execute access to all 13 probed installed files returned `STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED` (the files carry a conditional `WIN://SYSAPPID` ACE), while the same tool launched with `Invoke-CommandInDesktopPackage` loaded SetupEngine and deployed the pinned helper. Those diagnostics were observed live; their raw files were not retained. Local receipts for this run are retained privately.

### Historical signing fix: `d3a9bc46d10f4177dd9ad5d1b0fcfe32ffc315de`

Addresses the real P2 from the preceding `4947736e` review (3/3/3). Five actual-build regression cases pass: unsigned development resource allowed; default non-dev Release without signing input rejected; unsigned supplied input rejected; a valid existing OS-signed fixture embedded byte-for-byte with its signature retained; mismatched resource/input rejected. These build the actual SetupEngine project and inspect the actual compiled resource, not implementation text. No certificate, trust or installed runtime change was made.

The existing protected Azure signing account/profile signs the AnyCPU helper once, before every release consumer compiles SetupEngine. CI release tags/promotions require that artifact, including Store submissions whose outer package is unsigned. Expected OpenClaw signer identity is also checked before artifact upload and again in final release-payload verification.

**Limits:** Azure production signing was not executed locally. The OS-signed fixture proves the build/resource boundary, not production cleanup-host execution or signed AppLocker acceptance. Historical runtime and guest proof below retains its original source scope; references to "current-head" in that retained history mean `4947736e`, not this signing-fix head. Native ARM64, signed-policy acceptance and uninstall window-event finalization remain open. PR stays ready, not asserted merge-ready.

### Expanded disposable Windows-host execution, 2026-10-22

This later authorized execution supersedes the acquisition-only limits of the earlier attempt below, not its recorded failure. Provider/target/mode: **Hyper-V / windows / normal**; lease `cbx_ea5b9ce73e93`, VMID `490cc5f9-83b8-40e0-a733-5d03db32f1f6`, guest `WIN-A65IQ651TA1`, x64 Windows `10.0.29683`. No hosted run URL exists for this local Hyper-V run. Pinned Crabbox source `db7687e5`, executable SHA256 `587884DFACC22196889B7EFF5D593A080EAFE1730D4771A627F8E5CD11D6D5D3`. The previously live-qualified `1f79f365` desktop route was retained; the verified product difference to this pin was the Direct-readiness budget changing from five to ten minutes. Actual `warmup --desktop` succeeded in 296 seconds against the verified read-only differencing parent. Actual passive observation qualified session 1, WinSta0 Default/input Default with input-desktop access.

Official hash-verified portable .NET SDK `10.0.402` and PowerShell `7.6.7` were staged **only in the disposable guest**, under explicit authority. SDK first-use generated a guest development certificate; subsequent runs disabled that generation. No host installation, host certificate/policy, shared Gateway or parent-VHDX change occurred. All 54 transferred guest evidence files matched their guest SHA256. Outcomes below are sanitized copied receipts retained privately, not publicly downloadable local-path links.

Supported invocation vectors used, with the exact script selected per receipt:

```text
run --provider hyperv --target windows --windows-mode normal --id cbx_ea5b9ce73e93 --no-sync --script <exact artifact script path> --timing-json --timing-record off

```

Both used the trusted lease controller and pinned CLI, not an unsupported execution route. These are recorded command vectors, not instructions to replay expired authorization.
**1782 result at `4947736e6819c965107eb21a60cc0b9a6dbfb033`: actual enforced denial established; signed acceptance blocked.** The exact cleanup-host project and four owner/collector files were acquired from full-SHA public URLs with source/hash bindings. The actual project built x64 with `LangVersion=latest`, retaining PE version metadata. A nonexportable guest-local test signer signed the actual host and adjacent original worker/task scripts; source bindings, pre/post hashes and actual signatures were retained. Signing and trust were **guest-only test preparation, not production signing or reputation proof**.

A real **ENFORCING AppLocker Exe** collection, starting from actually empty baseline XML, scoped denial to the task restricted executables except the actual test publisher while allowing other execution. Effective policy was unchanged across the recorded second control. Actual unsigned start failed with native error **1260**, a real matching **8004** event identified the exact unsigned path and deny rule, and no forbidden sentinel effect occurred. The failed immediate-event collection and fresh 15-second subscription remain failures. A later finalizer attempted event reconciliation and signed-host launch, but transport expired: **signed acceptance remains UNVERIFIED**, not inferred from a valid signature.


This closes only the actual unsigned-denial observation, not the acceptance pair, full application-control diversity or any complete proof pool. No native uninstall scenario or finalized uninstall-window receipt was produced in this guest. Earlier Scheduler and qualified combined installed evidence remain separate. The PR remains READY (not draft); this evidence update does not declare it merge-ready.

**Transport and disposal:** the signed-acceptance finalizer and read-only desktop-actor probe each expired at 120 seconds; the final read-only normal `run --no-sync` recovery expired at 660 seconds. No output established their execution point. No further retries occurred. Final guest process/desktop cleanup before disposal is unverified. Parent exact-ID release completed at `2026-10-22T07:04:47.9589568Z`, exit 0, nonexpired. Independent `Get-VM` confirmed this exact VM absent; parent-template length and last-write UTC ticks were unchanged. No task-owned VM remains. VM disposal is not a claim that pre-teardown process cleanup passed.

### Overnight native-host proof attempt, 2026-10-22

This is an **infrastructure preflight failure, not a product test failure or pass**. The source head is unchanged. An authorized, unelevated native Windows Hyper-V desktop lease was requested from the approved read-only differencing parent. No managed/SDK/native application controls ran because the guest never reached readiness.

- Provider/target: `hyperv`, native `windows`, mode `normal`, desktop requested.
- Raw lease ID: `cbx_dd88578c30c0`.
- Run URL: not emitted; acquisition failed before a remote proof run existed.
- CLI pin: source `1a23239012e0906ecb82acb173f9855f6f53aa36`, Go1.27.3; local executable SHA-256 `F2036C256DB744AF00403D24193FECBDD09EA260696D2AF2D4752C1DBB13A69B`. This is an identified local interim build, not a claimed published Crabbox release.

Exact acquisition command (the CLI's normal credential handling was used; no credential value was read or printed):

```powershell
& 'E:\crabbox-proof\pins\1a232390-windows-hyperv\crabbox.exe' warmup --provider hyperv --target windows --windows-mode normal --hyperv-image 'E:\crabbox-proof\windows-readiness-template-v3\windows-primed-template.vhdx' --hyperv-switch 'Default Switch' --hyperv-user crabbox --desktop --keep --idle-timeout 45m --ttl 120m --timing-json
```

Copied acquisition result:

```text

stage=powershell-direct state=waiting budget=5m0s
guest readiness probe failed: exit status 1
context deadline exceeded
warmup exit=1; native controls executed=0
```

The cause beyond that PowerShell Direct/readiness failure remains unknown. It is not attributed to these PR changes, CPU load, credentials or desktop support without further evidence. No load-based start gate, elevation, checkpoint or unsupported `exec` command was used.

Exact cleanup command and independently checked outcome:

```text
crabbox stop --provider hyperv cbx_dd88578c30c0
stop exit=0
exact task VM absent=True
read-only parent length unchanged=True
read-only parent last-write UTC ticks unchanged=True
```

No other lease was stopped. The parent image was not hashed or modified. This evidence establishes the attempted environment and cleanup only; it does not qualify an interactive desktop, native startup behavior, signed execution or enforcement.

At the earlier acquisition-only stop, finalized signed-artifact uninstall-window observation and actual enforcing application-control execution were unverified; no policy or certificate was changed in that attempt. The later explicitly authorized guest-only signer/policy preparation and actual denial evidence above supersede that application-control acquisition limit; signed acceptance and uninstall-window proof remain unverified. Native ARM64 is unavailable. Existing current-head x64 Scheduler and separately labeled combined installed evidence retain their original scope; the failed host acquisition does not complete those missing cases.

Current-head hosted checks refreshed 2026-10-22T03:14:06.1175377Z: 11 skipped, 24 success. Existing per-test CI classifications elsewhere in this body remain unchanged; this preflight ran no product tests.

Current-head Windows x64 tests detect a deliberately visible classic console through WinEvent, periodic window enumeration and taskbar UI Automation. Helper A produces no visible-window or taskbar observations for worker exits 0 and 37; missing/throwing workers, complex paths and registration refresh are covered.

An additional current-head run used one uniquely named disposable Task Scheduler task, production helper deployment and production action registration/refresh, with a harmless event-synchronized worker. It detected the original direct PowerShell launch and observed no visible replacement launch. The copied output is below. This is actual Scheduler proof, **not installed-package or post-uninstall proof**.

Earlier three-run comparisons, including bounded light load, detected the original action and found zero visible-window/taskbar observations for A and a JScript prototype. Those comparisons are historical, not rerun JScript evidence on this head. A avoids adding WSH/JScript/COM policy dependencies.

Finite sampling cannot exclude every arbitrarily short transient. A desktop capture attempt did not reliably capture the console compositor surface, so no screenshot is presented as evidence of absence. The current-head behavioral observer and positive calibration are the supporting evidence.

Read-only rubber-duck review found no remaining correctness findings. [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/39472795642) of the earlier `d9e30f17` head found **no actionable code findings** (patch quality 4/6), but requested installed/upgrade/uninstall, ARM64 and application-control proof before merge (readiness 2/6). Installed task refresh, natural AFTER comparison, natural uninstall cleanup and fresh-agent restoration now have qualified combined-build evidence below. Uninstall window-event finalization, complete Hub-settings migration, native ARM64 and application-control gaps remain; before this bounded proof update, a new-head review had not been manually requested. One exact `@clawsweeper re-review` is authorized after body verification; draft state and reviewers remain unchanged.
